attributes.body_ja:
「なかなか」が肯定（こうてい）の文（ぶん）で使（つか）われると、物事（ものごと）の程度（ていど）が大（おお）きいことを表（あらわ）します。これが動詞（どうし）のナイ形（けい）（または「ありません」）と一緒（いっしょ）に否定（ひてい）の文（ぶん）で使（つか）われると、「思（おも）ったようにいかない」や「簡単（かんたん）には実現（じつげん）しない」のような意味（いみ）になります。多（おお）くの場合（ばあい）、この表現（ひょうげん）は話（はな）し手（て）が「本来（ほんらい）はそうなるはずだ」と思（おも）っているのに、簡単（かんたん）にはそうならないときに使（つか）われます。

「なかなか」（漢字（かんじ）は「中々（なかなか）」）は、文（ぶん）の始（はじ）まりか、動詞（どうし）の否定形（ひていけい）の前（まえ）に置（お）いて使（つか）います。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「中々（なかなか）」には「中（なか）」という漢字（かんじ）が含（ふく）まれるので、「なかなか〜ない」は、物事（ものごと）がちょうどいい位置（いち）（理想（りそう）の状態（じょうたい））に届（とど）いていないことを強調（きょうちょう）しているとイメージすると覚（おぼ）えやすいかもしれません。実際（じっさい）、「なかなか〜ない」は、思（おも）うようにいかずに、イライラしているときによく使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
When used positively, なかなか means to be 'very', or 'considerably' something. However, when used in a sentence that has a verb in the ない (or ありません) form, it carries the meaning of 'not at all', 'hardly', or 'far from'. Quite often, this expression is used to highlight something that the speaker expects should happen, but for some reason does/is not.

To use なかなか (or 中々（なかなか） in its kanji form), なかなか will be put at the beginning of a phrase (or directly before the negative verb), before further describing the situation.

Fun Fact

As 中々（なかなか） just means the 'middle' of something, this expression can be thought of as highlighting that something is not in the 'middle' (optimal place to achieve a certain result). Due to this, it often expresses that the speaker wants something to be in that 'optimal position' but feels frustration due to the fact that it isn't.

なかなか means 'quite' or 'fairly' when used with positive expressions, e.g. なかなか面白い映画だった ('It was quite an interesting movie.') In contrast, なかなか～ない expresses difficulty or delay, meaning 'not easily' or 'hardly', e.g. 仕事がなかなか終わらない ('The work just won't end.')

attributes.body: なかなか～ない and あまり～ない both express negation, but with different nuance. なかなか～ない implies difficulty or delay despite effort, e.g. なかなか話せない ('I can't speak easily.', implying difficulty despite effort). あまり～ない simply indicates a lower degree, e.g. あまり話せない ('I can't speak very much/well.').

attributes.body: Both negate expectations, but in different ways. 別に〜ない downplays something as not particularly important, e.g. 別に怒ってないよ ('I'm not especially mad.') なかなか〜ない indicates that something doesn't happen easily, e.g. なかなか怒らない人だね ('He's not someone who gets angry easily.')

attributes.body: Both express rarity or lack of frequency, but with different focus. 全く〜ない means something happens infrequently, e.g. 全く外食しない ('I hardly ever eat out.') なかなか〜ない suggests it doesn't happen easily or readily, often due to circumstances, e.g. 忙しくてなかなか外食できない ('I can't easily eat out because I'm so busy.')

attributes.body: めったに〜ない and なかなか〜ない both express rarity, but with different nuance. めったに〜ない means something rarely happens and carries a neutral or negative tone. なかなか〜ない, while also indicating rarity, emphasizes difficulty or persistence, often despite effort. It suggests that the situation is hard to bring about, rather than simply uncommon.

second_relatable.title: なかなか～ない
second_relatable.meaning: Not really, Hardly, Not easily or readily, By no means, Far from

attributes.body: なかなか～ない expresses that something is not easily done, often implying difficulty or repeated effort. For example, なかなかうまく話せない ('I just can't speak well.') has the nuance that the speaker is trying but not succeeding. In contrast, すこしも～ない means 'not even a little.' 少しも話せない means 'I can't speak at all.', focusing on the absence of ability without any implication of effort or struggle.
